Plots for ctJuliaFit objects

Source: R/ctJuliaBackend.R
plot.ctJuliaFit.Rd

Plots for a fit from backend='julia', as plot.ctStanFit gives for stan fits. 'regression' plots the model implied regression coefficients against the time interval (ctDiscretePars), 'kalman' plots expectations (ctPredict), 'priorcheck' plots each population parameter's prior and posterior (ctPlotPosterior), and 'trace' plots the optimiser's path to the estimate, or the chains of a sampled fit (ctTracePlot). The stan plot types 'density' and 'intervals' are not available, and 'priorcheck' shows the posterior densities instead.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'ctJuliaFit'
plot(x, types = "all", wait = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

x

Fit object from ctFit(..., backend='julia').

types

Vector of plot types: 'all', 'regression', 'kalman', 'priorcheck', 'trace'. 'all' leaves out 'regression' for a discrete time model, 'priorcheck' for a fit with no posterior draws, and 'trace' for a fit with nothing to trace.

wait

Logical. Pause between plots?

...

Passed through to ctDiscretePars and ctPredict. Beware clashes when types='all'.

Value

Nothing. Generates plots.

Examples

# \donttest{
# Needs a working julia backend, so the example is inert where Julia is
# absent -- including on CRAN, whose check machines have none.
if (isTRUE(ctJuliaStatus()$available)) {
  data <- ctstantestdat
  model <- ctModel(type = 'ct', manifestNames = 'Y1', latentNames = 'eta1',
    LAMBDA = matrix(1))
  model$pars$indvarying <- FALSE
  fit <- ctFit(data, model, backend = 'julia', cores = 1)
  plot(fit, wait = FALSE)
  # Julia keeps running between calls, holding what it has compiled;
  # this ends it.
  ctJuliaKill("session")
}
# }
